planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts after frost danger passes into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; this selection is propagated vegetatively rather than from seed.

directions: This selection of rigid verbena softens the species' usual magenta-purple to a paler, luminous lilac, held in the same three-branched candelabra clusters above dense clumps of rough, dark green, lance-shaped leaves. Set out in full sun in lean, sharply drained soil, since rich or damp ground encourages floppy growth and root rot over winter. Once established it spreads slowly by rhizomes and tolerates drought and poor soil with ease, blooming from early summer to the first hard frost. It holds up well in gravel gardens and at border edges where its low, dense habit and long bloom period draw bees and butterflies continuously.

common_name: Little One Verbena (Dwarf Upright Tall Verbena)

planting.note: Set out transplants after all danger of frost into average, well-drained soil in full sun; this patented selection is grown from nursery starts rather than seed.

directions: Unlike the low, spreading mound of 'Lollipop', this dwarf tall verbena keeps the species' upright, wiry-stemmed habit but stops at under two feet, so it reads as a true miniature rather than a groundcover form. Pinkish-purple buds open to pink flower clusters that fade nearly to white as they age, giving a two-tone effect over a long spring-to-frost bloom season. Grow in full sun in average to lean, well-drained soil; it is drought-tolerant once established and needs no staking thanks to its compact stature. Deadheading is rarely necessary since spent clusters are quickly hidden by new growth, and butterflies and bees visit continuously through the season.

common_name: Aztec Series Verbena (Compact Mounding Bedding Verbena)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost or set out plugs/nursery starts after frost danger passes into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: This vegetative series forms a low, dense, semi-trailing mound of small divided leaves covered in rounded clusters of lightly scented flowers across white, blue, pink, purple, and red shades. Grow in full sun in moderately fertile, moist but well-drained soil, watering to establish and then tapering off once roots fill the container or bed, since Aztec's strong powdery-mildew tolerance holds up best under drier conditions. Its compact size and heavy, continuous summer-to-frost bloom make it a standout in hanging baskets, window boxes, and border edging where taller verbena would flop. Pinch lightly after the first flush to keep the mound tight and encourage repeat flowering.

common_name: Quartz XP Series Verbena (Dwarf Mildew-Resistant Bedding Verbena)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before last frost, barely covering as seed needs darkness to germinate, then set out after frost danger passes into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: An AAS- and Fleuroselect-winning F1 series bred for a tight, mounded habit and large, domed flower clusters in red, violet-blue, salmon, and white, some with a contrasting white eye. Sow indoors in a dark, warm location since exposed seed germinates poorly, then transplant into full sun and moderately fertile, well-drained soil after frost. Its strong resistance to powdery mildew keeps foliage clean through hot, humid summers with minimal fungicide input, and its compact, uniform size suits the front of borders, edging, and mixed containers. Deadhead spent clusters occasionally to keep bloom dense from summer into autumn.
